title: Consolidate crypto libraries, upgrade TLS stack, and remediate SAML assertion edge cases
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Reduce tech debt and security risk by consolidating JWT/JOSE libraries across services, upgrading the platform TLS/OpenSSL stack to a modern, supported baseline, and applying a targeted remediation for a SAML XML signature canonicalization edge case that causes intermittent assertion validation failures.

Background: Over the last 18 months several services have independently adopted different JWT/JOSE implementations (go-jose, node-jsonwebtoken, python-jose forks) and a mix of OpenSSL 1.1.x and 3.0 builds across environments. This has led to divergent behavior for JWK handling (kid matching, alg fallback), inconsistent TLS defaults (TLS1.2 vs TLS1.3 negotiation preferences), and at least two incidents where SAML assertions that included redundant XML whitespace or unusual namespaces failed validation in production (customer SSO flows for enterprise accounts).

Goals:
- Standardize on a small set of vetted JOSE libraries for each runtime (Go, Node, Python) to reduce surface area for vulnerabilities and inconsistent token parsing.
- Upgrade OpenSSL across the platform images to 3.0.8 (or later stable) and enforce TLS1.3-first cipher suites in runtime configs, with fallbacks for legacy partner integrations.
- Patch and upstream a fix for the SAML canonicalization/whitespace handling bug in the python-saml wrapper we use, while providing a short-term compatibility shim.
- Create automated tests (unit + integration + fuzz) that exercise malformed SAML assertions and JWS/JWT edge cases to prevent regressions.
acceptance_criteria: All core backend services use approved JOSE libraries (Go: go-jose v2.6+, Node: jose v4+, Python: python-jose maintained fork) and token validation test suite passes
Platform base images and dedicated runtime pools use OpenSSL 3.x; CI matrices exercise TLS1.3 negotiation and TLS1.2 fallback paths
SAML canonicalization fix merged and published (upstream PR number included) and enterprise SSO flows validated in staging for 3 customers
Automated fuzz tests for SAML assertions added to nightly CI and a regression alert configured in Console when assertion failures spike
Performance regression within +/- 5% of baseline for token validation hot paths; if >5% we have mitigation plan (caching/accelerators) and documented tradeoffs
comments: 2025-02-05 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after two customer SSO failures and internal audit calling out mixed OpenSSL versions. Initial triage recommends a consolidation + upgrade approach rather than ad-hoc patches.

2025-02-10 - Liam OConnor: Ran library inventory across services. Findings: 12 services using 5 different JWT libraries; 7 images still on OpenSSL 1.1.1; python-saml wrapper (vendor/my-saml) has failing canonicalization for namespaced elements. Added project plan and risk matrix to Confluence.

2025-02-15 - Security Review (Sophie Tran): Reviewed proposed libraries. flagged go-jose v2.6+ and jose v4+ as acceptable. Recommended adding continuous dependency scanning and enabling FIPS-aware build flags for Private deployments. Marked security_review_required=true.

2025-02-20 - Devs (Liam): Implemented a compatibility shim for SAML validator to normalize redundant whitespace and namespace prefixes in staging. Verified with a corpus of 200+ captured failing assertions (from sandboxed customers). Patch is temporary until upstream fix merges.

2025-02-24 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4872 - 'standardize-jwt-libraries-and-add-token-test-suite' (review in progress). CI failures show one legacy partner token with non-standard 'alg' header; created sub-issue ENG-20679 to support partner fallback.

2025-02-27 - Performance check (infra): upgrading OpenSSL in base image increased handshake CPU by ~3% in microbenchmarks for mutual TLS; KV cache hits reduced overall request CPU. We'll instrument token validation hotspots to identify further optimizations.

2025-03-02 - Upstream: Submitted upstream PR to python-saml fork addressing canonicalization (PR: https://github.com/onelogin/python-saml/pull/312). Preparing release tag for internal use while upstream review completes. Next steps: schedule canary rollout for devnet, then staging, then gradual prod rollout with monitoring.
